questions.question: Which statement about the relationship between TR46 (2024 revision) and PDA TR39 is correct?

options.A: TR46 replaces TR39; both address the same manufacturer-side transport issues and share the same validation approach
options.B: TR46 supplements TR39, addressing issues beyond the manufacturer and focusing on the last mile of distribution
options.C: TR46 regulates only the customs clearance procedures for imported drugs, while TR39 regulates domestic distribution and warehouse management
options.D: TR46 is an appendix to TR39 and provides only the specifications and calibration requirements for temperature recorders

questions.explanation: TR46 describes itself as a document that supplements TR39 (shipping of temperature-controlled drugs), aiming to go beyond manufacturer-side issues and address problems specific to the last mile. The 2024 revision updates the original 2009 edition to reflect more regulations, newer technologies and more complex supply chains.

questions.question: How does TR46 define the "last mile"?

options.A: The final leg of transport of raw materials from the supplier to the manufacturing site, usually arranged by the raw material supplier
options.B: The transfer within the manufacturing site from the warehouse to the packaging facility, which falls within internal distribution
options.C: The bulk transport of full pallets of finished product from the manufacturer to the wholesaler, mainly by full container or truckload
options.D: The final transfer of the drug from the manufacturer or wholesaler to the end user (the patient, or an entity such as a pharmacy or hospital)

questions.explanation: TR46 defines the last mile as the final transfer of the drug from the manufacturer or wholesaler to the end user, who may be the patient or an entity that supplies the drug to the patient (for example, a pharmacy or hospital). The earlier the link, the better the organization knows the product and the greater its resources, so the last mile especially needs guidance.

questions.question: According to the TR46 glossary, what is Mean Kinetic Temperature (MKT)?

options.A: A single calculated isothermal temperature at which the amount of degradation equals the total degradation occurring at the fluctuating temperatures
options.B: The simple arithmetic mean of all temperature readings over a period, without considering the effect of temperature on the degradation rate
options.C: The difference between the highest and lowest temperatures recorded during the monitoring period, used to express the magnitude of fluctuation
options.D: The midpoint of the product's labeled storage temperature range, used to set the upper and lower alarm limits

questions.explanation: MKT represents the total degradation effect of non-isothermal storage with a single calculated temperature, and can be viewed as the isothermal storage temperature that simulates the effect of temperature variation. TR46 stresses that it is not a simple arithmetic mean, because degradation is faster at high temperatures, which gives them more weight in the result.

questions.question: In the TR46 glossary, which kind of record is a true copy (also called a certified copy)?

options.A: Any scanned copy saved as a file, as long as the content is clear and readable
options.B: The file or format in which the data were originally generated, such as a handwritten original observation record or raw instrument output, that has not undergone any verification or certification
options.C: A copy that has been verified to be identical and complete compared with the original record, with electronic data including the necessary metadata and the original format
options.D: A backup file made periodically to prevent data loss and stored at another secure location, with content that is not necessarily identical to the original record

questions.explanation: A true copy is a copy that has been verified and certified to be identical and complete compared with the original record, with electronic data retaining the necessary metadata and (where applicable) the original format. The option about the file or format in which the data were first generated and not yet verified describes the original record; a plain scan or a backup has not necessarily been verified and certified.

questions.question: According to the TR46 glossary, what is the difference between corrective action and preventive action in CAPA?

options.A: Corrective action addresses a nonconformity that has occurred and prevents recurrence; preventive action prevents a problem that has not yet occurred
options.B: Corrective action addresses a risk that has not yet occurred, aiming at prevention in advance; preventive action addresses a deviation that has already occurred
options.C: They differ in name only; the content, timing of initiation and purpose are completely identical, and they can be used interchangeably
options.D: Corrective action is carried out by the customer; preventive action is carried out by the regulatory authority

questions.explanation: CAPA is action to eliminate the cause of a detected nonconformity or other undesirable situation. Corrective action is to prevent recurrence, and preventive action is to prevent occurrence.

questions.question: TR46 divides drug distribution into internal and external distribution. Which statement about external distribution is correct?

options.A: The goods are still held by the MAH, and inspectors check it only as part of the manufacturer's GMP inspection, without separate GDP oversight
options.B: It includes only transport from the manufacturing site to the packaging site and warehouse; the goods still flow within the manufacturer, involving no distributor or wholesaler
options.C: The goods no longer belong to the manufacturer; it covers distribution from the distribution center to wholesalers, retailers, clinics or patients, overseen by inspectors under GDP authorization
options.D: It is usually part of the product application and is not subject to GDP, being managed only under the marketing authorization conditions, and no distributor needs to hold a GDP authorization

questions.explanation: Internal distribution is within the manufacturer's supply chain, where the MAH always owns the goods, and it is inspected under the manufacturer's GMP/GDP authorization. External distribution is transport of goods that no longer belong to the manufacturer; it is usually not part of the product application and is overseen by inspectors under the wholesaler's GDP authorization.

questions.topic: First mile vs last mile characteristics
questions.question: Compared with the first mile, what is typically characteristic of last mile transport?

options.A: The quantity increases to full pallet shipments, often long-distance intercontinental transport, with longer transit times
options.B: The quantity shrinks to a single box or a few packages with few items, and distance and time are shorter, although remote areas may still need several days
options.C: A single shipment typically carries a mix of more than one hundred products, which is the most typical characteristic of the last mile, with the longest transit time
options.D: Distance and quantity are unchanged and only the mode of transport changes from aircraft to truck, with the same temperature control requirements

questions.explanation: TR46 notes that from the first mile to the last mile, quantity shrinks from full pallets to single packages, and the number of items goes from one or a few, to hundreds in the middle mile, and back to one or a few in the last mile, with distance and time also shortening. The exception is remote areas, where the last mile may take several days if it relies on walking or river transport. Mixed loads of hundreds of products are characteristic of the middle mile.

questions.question: Among the supply chain roles listed in TR46, which one is responsible for checking regulatory compliance and issuing the permits that allow the MAH to import drugs into a particular market?

options.A: Third-Party Logistic Provider (3PL)
options.B: Point of Dispensing
options.C: Customs
options.D: Inspectorate

questions.explanation: The Inspectorate checks whether manufacturers, wholesalers, pharmacies or processors comply with the relevant regulations and issues the permits that allow the MAH to import drugs into a particular market. Customs is responsible for levying import duties; a 3PL carries out logistics operations such as warehousing and transport on behalf of the manufacturer or wholesaler; the Point of Dispensing is the location where drugs are dispensed to users.

questions.question: According to TR46's description of the EU GDP transport chapter, how should a temperature excursion during transport be handled?

options.A: It should be reported to the distributor and the recipient of the affected product; the temperature control information comes from the manufacturer or the outer packaging label
options.B: It must be reported only when it exceeds the range permitted by stability data; a minor excursion needs only an internal record
options.C: It needs only an internal record and the recipient need not be informed, with the distributor deciding afterwards whether to sample and test
options.D: The recipient decides whether to use the product, with no need to report to the distributor or manufacturer, and no written record is needed

questions.explanation: EU GDP requires that the storage conditions stated by the manufacturer or on the outer packaging be maintained during transport, and when a temperature excursion occurs it should be reported to the distributor and the recipient of the affected product. Because EU GDP does not further require stability data, any excursion indicated by a temperature indicator must be reported, rather than only those beyond the stability range.

questions.question: TR46 uses the reorganization of Zambia's public supply chain as an example. What did the reorganization do?

options.A: Added more regional warehouses so that every province has one, kept all the original regional warehouses and increased the months of stock at each tier, to shorten the delivery distance to each province
options.B: Moved all drug distribution to private wholesalers, closed all public warehouses and had suppliers hold the stock on consignment, to reduce the operating costs of the public sector
options.C: Eliminated the district warehouses, expanded the central and regional warehouses, sited them by population and geography (at most about eight hours' drive), and introduced central inventory management
options.D: Kept the original three-tier network, only increasing the months of safety stock at each tier and adding a tier of provincial transfer stations to cope with changing demand in each region

questions.explanation: Zambia changed its original Tier-3 network to a model closer to the last mile: eliminating district warehouses, expanding the central and regional warehouses, and delivering directly from the central warehouse and six regional warehouses to 3400 health facilities, with regional warehouse locations decided by population, geography and distance to the facilities (at most eight hours' drive), and building a central IT inventory management system across the whole chain. The results were shorter distances, lower total inventory and improved access to drugs.

questions.question: According to TR46's description of Brazil's RDC 430/2020, what is the scope of shipping qualification?

options.A: It applies only to temperature-sensitive drugs and only to cold chain products; ambient drugs do not need shipping qualification
options.B: It applies to all drugs (not only temperature-sensitive products), using a risk-based approach
options.C: It applies only to imported drugs; domestically produced and distributed drugs are outside the scope
options.D: It applies only to vaccines in the public supply chain; private channels and other drugs are not covered

questions.explanation: RDC 430/2020 (amended by RDC 653/2022) requires temperature mapping of transport routes, temperature monitoring during transport, and shipping qualification for all drugs (not only temperature-sensitive products), using a risk-based approach.

questions.question: In Brazil, when the MAH entrusts a third-party company with distribution or logistics services, how is liability divided under RDC 234/2018?

options.A: The contracted company is jointly liable with the contracting company for the technical and operational aspects of that activity
options.B: The contracted company bears full liability and the MAH is exempt, needing only to keep the contract on file
options.C: The MAH bears full liability, and the contracted company is not responsible for the technical and operational aspects and only follows instructions
options.D: The receiving hospital or pharmacy bears liability, and neither contracting party is responsible for distribution quality

questions.explanation: TR46 notes that the MAH may outsource distribution or logistics services to a third party under RDC 234/2018, in which case the contracted company is jointly and severally liable with the contracting company for the technical and operational aspects inherent to that activity.

questions.topic: US — regulatory gap and USP chapters
questions.question: What does TR46 say about US regulation of packaging and shipping of temperature-controlled drugs?

options.A: 21 CFR 203 and 205 specify in detail the methods for packaging and shipping temperature-controlled products, including validation frequency and packaging material specifications
options.B: Only FDA GMP regulates shipping, USP does not address it, and states set no separate requirements, certifications or shipping validation requirements for wholesalers
options.C: All states require wholesalers to hold the same shipping validation certification, issued and audited uniformly by the FDA, and the certification must be reapplied for and renewed every year
options.D: 21 CFR 203/205 do not specify packaging and shipping, but USP <659> and <1079> provide guidance, the latter covering last mile participants

questions.explanation: Neither 21 CFR 203 nor 205 addresses packaging and shipping requirements for temperature-controlled products. USP <659> and <1079> (both revised in 2020) provide clear guidance, and the scope of <1079> extends beyond manufacturers to all last mile participants, including wholesalers, distributors, pharmacies, hospitals and logistics service providers.

questions.question: A US wholesaler is going to ship a refrigerated drug, but the manufacturer has not provided packaging requirements or stability data supporting conditions beyond the label. According to TR46, how should the wholesaler proceed?

options.A: Because regulation does not explicitly require it, ship in ordinary packaging as long as delivery is within a reasonable time, without obtaining further data from the manufacturer
options.B: Wait for patient complaints before deciding whether to adjust the packaging, using complaint records as the basis, without first evaluating the temperature risk
options.C: Use validated packaging or shipping methods that maintain the labeled storage conditions from the time the product leaves the temperature-controlled environment until delivery to the customer, and have the data on file
options.D: Always switch to air freight, with no packaging validation data needed, because shorter transit time guarantees the temperature, and no proof of storage conditions is needed

questions.explanation: Without explicit packaging requirements or manufacturer stability data, a distributor can only follow the manufacturer's instructions and should use validated packaging or shipping methods so that the product maintains the labeled storage conditions from leaving the temperature-controlled environment until delivery to the customer, and the distributor is responsible for having data that demonstrate this.

questions.question: What does TR46 say about the US NABP Drug Distributor Accreditation program?

options.A: It is a mandatory federal scheme in which all wholesalers must undergo on-site audits and be recertified every year, with audit results published every year
options.B: Since January 2022 it no longer requires on-site audits, and instead uses a voluntary supply chain inspection; nearly half of the states require licensed distributors to hold it
options.C: It applies only to distributors with physical facilities in the state and not to out-of-state or online distributors, and requires quarterly on-site audits
options.D: It replaces state licenses; holding the accreditation removes the need for a state license and allows direct operation nationwide, and can replace all federal-level permits

questions.explanation: The NABP Drug Distributor Accreditation was restructured in January 2022 and no longer requires on-site visits, instead conducting a voluntary supply chain inspection of the facility's procedures and practices. Nearly half of the states require licensed distributors to obtain this accreditation (whether or not they have a facility in that state), and some states (such as Florida) have stricter licensing procedures.

questions.question: A Canadian wholesaler contracts a 3PL to warehouse drugs. According to TR46, what must the wholesaler ensure?

options.A: As long as the 3PL has its own business license, it need not be listed on the wholesaler's Drug Establishment Licence (DEL)
options.B: As long as the 3PL's building is registered with the provincial government, it need not be listed in the wholesaler's licence annex
options.C: The 3PL's warehouse building need only comply with local fire and building codes, and the storage conditions are decided by the 3PL
options.D: The 3PL's building is listed in the DEL warehouse annex, and the 3PL stores the drugs under the labeled conditions

questions.explanation: Canada requires every building in which drugs are stored to be listed in the warehouse annex of the DEL. When a 3PL is used, the wholesaler is responsible for ensuring that the 3PL's building is listed and that the 3PL stores according to the labeled conditions. The design, validation and per-route confirmation against protocol of packaging and package configurations are the responsibility of the DEL holder.

questions.question: A pharmacy's refrigerator stopped cooling over a weekend, causing a prolonged temperature excursion. According to TR46 §4.2, what is the better way to use MKT to evaluate this excursion?

options.A: For longer segments (such as storage), calculate the MKT of the excursion period only rather than of the whole segment; for short segments such as transport, pair it with the manufacturer's upper and lower temperature limits
options.B: Always evaluate with the MKT of the entire storage period, to avoid overestimating the impact of the excursion, and use it to decide whether the product can be used, without distinguishing the period in which the excursion occurred
options.C: As long as the MKT is below the upper limit of the labeled range, the product can be shipped directly to patients, without referring to the manufacturer's stability data and without evaluating how long the excursion lasted
options.D: MKT cannot be used to evaluate excursions; only the maximum temperature can be used, and any reading outside the range must lead to destruction, with no statistical tools used for evaluation

questions.explanation: TR46 explains that for short segments (such as transport), MKT is best used together with the manufacturer's upper and lower temperature limits; for longer segments (such as storage), calculating the MKT of the excursion period itself is more appropriate than using the whole segment. Disposition still needs to be confirmed with the manufacturer or MAH that holds the stability data, and each link can interpret only the segment for which it is responsible.

questions.question: A mail-order pharmacy is choosing a thermal protection solution for refrigerated drugs delivered the next day. According to TR46, how should the duration for thermal qualification be calculated?

options.A: Count only the time on the delivery vehicle, about 12 hours, because the package needs no temperature control at the distribution center, excluding storage and transfer links
options.B: From early on the day of shipping until the carrier delivers to the home door, excluding the wait before the user opens the package, and without needing to cover abnormal delay scenarios
options.C: From the packing of the first package until the user opens it; for next-day delivery it needs to cover 36 hours, and in practice often longer
options.D: From the package's arrival at the distribution center until the courier obtains a signature, covering only standard transit time and excluding the final home delivery stage

questions.explanation: TR46 states that the duration of thermal qualification should run from the packing of the first package until the end user opens it. For next-day delivery, it must cover packing, delivery to the door or mailbox, and the time until the patient opens it after work, about 36 hours, and the document also cautions that the actual time needed is often longer.

questions.question: Comparing data loggers with temperature indicators, which statement is correct?

options.A: Indicators provide a complete temperature record and statistical analysis, whereas loggers provide only a pass or fail result; their functions are exactly opposite
options.B: Loggers provide complete temperature data and statistical analysis; indicators are cheaper, only confirm whether the range was maintained, and do not show the time of the excursion
options.C: Neither needs calibration, because they are used only as a rough reference and not as a basis for release or disposition, so their accuracy need not be periodically checked
options.D: The sensor should be placed on the surface of the outer packaging to represent ambient temperature, rather than near the product or at the hottest and coldest points, without regard to the location of hot or cold spots

questions.explanation: A logger provides complete temperature data for the whole shipment (including statistics such as recording interval and cumulative time outside limits); an indicator is a lower-cost alternative that only confirms whether the temperature range was maintained and usually does not show the time of the excursion. TR46 also requires devices to be calibrated (accuracy of at least ±0.5 °C) and the sensor to be placed next to the product, which best represents product temperature.

questions.question: According to TR46's contract management requirements, what conditions must a contract-acceptor meet if it wants to pass the entrusted work on to a third party?

options.A: It need only notify the contract-giver, without approval, and provide a list of third parties afterwards for the record
options.B: As long as the third party holds a GDP certificate it can be subcontracted directly, without evaluation or audit by the contract-giver
options.C: The contract-acceptor may decide on its own, the contract-giver need only keep a record afterwards, and the contract-acceptor arranges the audit itself
options.D: It must first be evaluated and approved by the contract-giver, and the third party must be audited by the contract-giver or the contract-acceptor

questions.explanation: TR46 requires a written contract between the contract-giver and the contract-acceptor that clearly defines the responsibilities of each party, with a separate technical or quality agreement in addition to the commercial contract (covering deviation management and change control). The contract-acceptor may not pass work to a third party until the contract-giver has evaluated and approved it and the third party has been audited, and must pass on to the contract-giver any information that may affect product quality.

questions.question: TR46 compares data retention provisions in EU GDP, WHO and the UK. Which statement is correct?

options.A: EU GDP: backup data are kept for at least five years in accordance with national regulations, at a separate secure location
options.B: WHO: all monitoring records are kept for at least five years
options.C: UK: the retention period is product shelf life plus one year, and backup data are set separately by national regulations
options.D: EU GDP: backup data may be kept at the same location as the original system, and the retention period is set by the company

questions.explanation: EU GDP requires regular backups, with backup data retained in accordance with national regulations for at least five years and stored at a separate and secure location. The WHO requirement is that monitoring records be kept for at least product shelf life plus one year (or as national regulations require); the UK requires two years, after which records may be destroyed.

questions.question: An audit finds that distribution center employees share one system account and password. According to TR46 §6.1.3, how should this be handled?

options.A: Simply remind employees not to share any more, without recording it, investigating whether any data have been altered, or notifying anyone
options.B: Deal with it only when a product quality problem occurs or the next audit finds it again, with no regular review of accounts and permission settings and no recording as a deviation
options.C: Treat it as a data integrity breach: record a deviation, investigate the root cause and set a CAPA; if quality is affected, escalate to management and notify customers
options.D: Let the IT department handle it on its own, without Quality involvement, simply changing the password and notifying the direct supervisor, with no notification of customers or any external party

questions.explanation: TR46 lists shared accounts or passwords as one example of a data integrity breach. Any detected or potential breach must be recorded as a deviation, with the root cause investigated and a CAPA set; if it may affect product quality or patient safety, it must be escalated to management, customers must be notified, and the competent authority must be notified in accordance with local regulations.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the five basic principles of temperature management listed in TR46?

options.A: Temperature data need to be kept only when an excursion occurs, and normal monitoring data may be deleted after release
options.B: Temperature is measured with calibrated sensors at the hot or cold spot locations identified by temperature mapping
options.C: The disposition of products with temperature excursions is decided by the recipient, without following GDP procedures or the distributor's deviation management
options.D: Temperature specifications need to be set only for the finished product, without covering the process, transport and storage systems

questions.explanation: The five principles are: set temperature specifications for the product, process and system; control the environment with validated active or passive systems; measure with calibrated sensors at the hot or cold spot locations identified by temperature mapping; retain data in accordance with ALCOA+; and investigate temperature excursions and carry out disposition under GDP. The other options are contrary to the principles.

questions.question: When a pharmacist in the EU scans the 2D code on a pack, the system shows that the serial number has already been decommissioned. According to TR46, how should the pharmacist handle this?

options.A: The pack may be dispensed directly to the patient, because a serial number need only be scanned once, and the decommissioned status in the system is for reference only, with no notification of any party
options.B: Re-register the serial number as active on their own, then dispense it to the patient and record the deviation afterwards, without notifying the national competent authority
options.C: Return it to the wholesaler without notification, keeping no record of the pack and deciding on their own whether to destroy it
options.D: Quarantine the pack until the matter is clarified; suspected falsified medicines must be reported to the national competent authority and handled under an approved written procedure

questions.explanation: In the EU, pharmacists check the anti-tampering device and scan the 2D code to decommission the serial number before dispensing. If the alert shows that the serial number does not exist or has been decommissioned, or the anti-tampering device has been broken, the pack must be quarantined until the matter is clarified, and suspected falsified medicines must be reported to the national competent authority and handled under an approved written procedure.

questions.question: TR46 recommends setting a baseline and a target for each last mile performance indicator. How do their purposes differ?

options.A: A baseline is for comparison with external benchmarks; a target is for comparison with past performance; the two are not interchangeable, and both should be reviewed every year
options.B: They are the same, differing only in wording, and either may be used according to each unit's habit, with no need to set values or trend thresholds separately or to compare with past performance regularly
options.C: A baseline is compared with past performance; a target may be an internal or external benchmark, compared with expected performance; root cause analysis should be considered when it is not met
options.D: A baseline is used only for temperature data and a target only for on-time delivery rate, and the two cannot be used for other indicators, with no comparison against external benchmarks or past performance

questions.explanation: Each indicator should have a target (which may be an internal or external benchmark) and a baseline. The baseline lets you compare with previous performance, and the target lets you compare with expected performance. If a target is persistently not met, or a trend signals a possible problem, root cause analysis should be considered and, as appropriate, a corrective action plan started.

questions.question: What does TR46 say about the cost of emergency stockpiles?

options.A: A static stockpile does not need rotation, so it carries no expiry risk and is the lowest-cost approach, needing no contract and no consideration of destruction costs
options.B: If the stockpile is not rotated with regular inventory, the risk of expiry is high, causing destruction costs and a total loss of the investment; who bears the cost should be agreed in the contract
options.C: A wholesaler can easily hold large stockpiles of more than two weeks because margins are high and costs are negligible, with no need to consider expiry and destruction costs
options.D: A dynamic stockpile cannot use FEFO and can only use first-in-first-out, and must be managed completely separately from regular inventory, with no responsibilities needing to be agreed in a contract

questions.explanation: A static stockpile that is not rotated with regular inventory has a high risk of expiry, leading to destruction costs, loss of the investment and environmental impact, and who bears the expiry and destruction costs should be defined in the contract. Including buffer stock in the wholesaler's rotating inventory and applying FEFO is a dynamic stockpile; but for a wholesaler to hold large stockpiles of more than two weeks is quite difficult because of the cost of capital and insufficient margins.

questions.question: What is the concept of Extended Producer (Product) Responsibility (EPR) in TR46?

options.A: Only the end user is responsible for discarding the packaging, and upstream manufacturers and distributors bear no responsibility, with no need to consider it at the design stage
options.B: Only packaging material manufacturers need to take back the packaging materials they produce, and other links need not take part, excluding downstream use and disposal
options.C: It applies only to the destruction of the drug itself, not the packaging, and does not involve material selection or processes, with no need to consider recovery and reuse of packaging
options.D: Every link in the product chain shares responsibility for the environmental impact of packaging, from upstream materials and processes to downstream use, waste management and disposal

questions.explanation: The EPR concept is that every link in the product chain shares the environmental impact of packaging, covering upstream material selection and manufacturing through to downstream use, waste management and disposal. The EU has made EPR public policy, requiring packaging producers to be financially and practically responsible for the post-use stage of the product, for example the Green Dot scheme.

questions.question: TR46 lists two reverse logistics models for drugs: closed-loop transit and return of packaging. What is the difference?

options.A: Closed-loop is when the wholesaler delivers with its own trucks and takes back old packaging; return of packaging is when the shipment includes a prepaid postage label for the user to send it back
options.B: Closed-loop is when the user sends the packaging back themselves; return of packaging is when the wholesaler delivers with its own trucks and takes back the packaging
options.C: Both are used only for the destruction of expired drugs and have nothing to do with packaging recovery or reuse, the difference being only transport distance
options.D: Closed-loop applies only to cold chain products such as vaccines; return of packaging applies only to oral tablets and capsules

questions.explanation: Closed-loop transit is common among wholesalers in Europe and the US, which deliver to end users with their own trucks and bring old packaging back to be returned to the channel or recycled. In return of packaging, a prepaid postage label is included or attached to the original shipment so that the user can send the packaging back after taking out the drugs; this method can also be used to return expired or improperly disposed drugs.

questions.question: When comparing a traditional EPS box with water-based coolant against a VIP with PCM passive temperature control solution, what does TR46 say?

options.A: VIP with PCM is usually cheaper, so it should be preferred, and freight has little effect on total cost, so no other costs need to be evaluated
options.B: Freight is not an important factor in choosing a solution; only the unit price of the box and the cost of the coolant need to be compared, without considering volume and weight
options.C: VIP with PCM is usually more expensive; the traditional solution is bulky and heavy, so freight is higher, and freight is often greater than the cost of the temperature control solution itself
options.D: The traditional solution is smaller, so freight is lower, making it the lowest-cost solution in every case, with no need to compare total cost, irrespective of differences in packaging weight and freight

questions.explanation: TR46 states that a passive solution made of VIP and PCM is usually more expensive than a traditional EPS box with water-based coolant; the traditional solution is larger and heavier for the same payload, which increases freight. Freight is usually greater than the cost of the temperature control solution itself and significantly affects total transport cost, so the unit price of the packaging cannot be the only comparison.

questions.question: In the business contingency plan recommended by TR46, what is the practice regarding data and information systems?

options.A: Back up data and IT infrastructure at a remote location outside the area expected to be affected by a disaster
options.B: Keep the backup on another floor of the same building, so that it can be quickly accessed and restored when a disaster occurs
options.C: Back up only paper records; electronic data and system configurations need no backup, because the supplier can provide them again
options.D: After a disaster occurs, decide the backup approach and restoration order according to the actual losses

questions.explanation: One key point of a business continuity plan is to back up data and IT infrastructure at a remote location outside the area expected to be affected by a disaster. Other recommendations include prioritizing operations in advance, preparing alternative operating sites, planning transport rerouting, designating alternate personnel, and establishing notification and response mechanisms.
